questions.stem: A disjunct holds the row x - y <= 0, with bounds 0 <= x <= 40 and 10 <= y <= 30. Which M does gdp.bigm give that row?

options.text: 40, the upper bound of x alone
options.says: M must cover the largest value of the row's left side, x - y, which uses both variables' bounds.

options.text: 30, the largest gap the two bounds allow
options.says: Right: 40 - 10 = 30, as M = 12 on the outage rows was the most s_i + d_i - s_j can be.

options.text: 70, the sum of the two upper bounds
options.says: The row's left side is x - y; y's upper bound lowers it, so the sum of the upper bounds is not the left side's largest value.

options.text: None, since gdp.bigm needs a bigM argument
options.says: gdp.bigm computes M from the variables' bounds; bigM= is needed only when a bound is missing.

origin.section: gdp.bigm Writes the Big-M Rows and Finds M From the Bounds

questions.stem: An analyst wants the hull LP bound of a GDP model. The script applies core.relax_integer_vars, then gdp.hull, then solves. What number comes back?

options.text: The hull LP bound, since the order does not matter
options.says: Relaxing first found no binaries; on the outage jobs this order printed 17.00, the MILP optimum, not 13.98.

options.text: The big-M LP bound, since relaxing undoes the hull
options.says: The hull rows were written; what stayed integer were its binaries, so the result was 17.00, not the big-M bound 10.00.

options.text: An error, since gdp.hull needs integer variables
options.says: The script runs; the lesson's program printed 17.00 for this order.

options.text: The MILP optimum, since the binaries come later
options.says: Right: the transformation creates the binaries, so relaxing first leaves them binary; transform, then relax.

origin.section: gdp.hull Writes a Copy per Disjunct and Needs Every Variable Bounded

questions.stem: A disjunct mentions a variable z with lower bound 0 and no upper bound. Which transformation can still turn the model into a MILP?

options.text: gdp.bigm, given an M by hand with its bigM argument
options.says: Right: without a bound gdp.bigm raises GDP_Error, but apply_to(m, bigM=20) solved; the M is then unchecked.

options.text: gdp.hull, since it copies z for each disjunct
options.says: The hull caps each copy by z's bound times the switch, so it raised GDP_Error for the missing bound, and it has no bigM escape.

options.text: Neither, since both need z bounded and take no M
options.says: gdp.bigm takes a hand-given M with bigM=; the lesson's program solved that way.

options.text: Both, since each one estimates its own bound for z
options.says: Neither estimates a missing bound: both raised GDP_Error on the outage model with one bound removed.
